books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

stimulus.source_note: Uncle Sam’s Youngest Son, Citizen Know Nothing (Sarony & Co., lithograph, New York, 1854). Library of Congress, LCCN2003689281. Public domain.
stimulus.text: A lithograph published in New York in 1854, titled “Uncle Sam’s Youngest Son, Citizen Know Nothing.” It shows a young man in a wide-brimmed hat, wrapped in an American flag, with a plaque reading “CITIZEN” below him and an eagle above.

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: The cartoon’s title and the flag wrapped around the young man most directly present the Know-Nothing as

options.text: a recent immigrant proud of his new home.
options.misconception: The figure is Uncle Sam’s “youngest son,” born to the nation, not a newcomer; the cartoon claims native birth, not immigrant pride.
Nothing in the image touches slavery or the plantation; the flag and the word “Citizen” point to nativism, not to the South.

options.text: a native-born American, the truest kind of citizen.
a Catholic priest leading his congregation.
options.misconception: Background from the books: Know-Nothings attacked Catholic immigrants; the cartoon’s hero is the native-born Protestant, not a priest.

rationales.A: The figure is Uncle Sam’s “youngest son,” born to the nation, not a newcomer; the cartoon claims native birth, not immigrant pride.
rationales.B: Nothing in the image touches slavery or the plantation; the flag and the word “Citizen” point to nativism, not to the South.
rationales.C: Wrapped in the flag and named Uncle Sam’s son, the figure claims that true citizenship belongs to the native-born.
rationales.D: Background from the books: Know-Nothings attacked Catholic immigrants; the cartoon’s hero is the native-born Protestant, not a priest.
rationales.general:
1. Read the title first: “Uncle Sam’s Youngest Son” claims a family tie to America itself.
2. Add the picture: the flag wraps the young man, and “CITIZEN” is stamped below him.
3. Put the two together: the cartoon says the native-born man is the real American.
Remember: a cartoon’s title often states its argument; read it before the picture.
